facts.fact: The health ministry's PS-SNISS 2020-2024 (February 2021) states that since 2016 the routine data of the local health information system (SLIS, from CSCOM, CSRéf, garrison infirmaries and some private and faith facilities), the hospital information system (SIH) and epidemic alert (SAE) are all on the DHIS2 platform, with 2019 completeness of data forms, sourced to DHIS2, of 99.7% for SLIS, 99.1% for SIH and 95.7% for SAE, and timeliness of entry into DHIS2 of 63% at the first deadline for SLIS and 64% for SIH.

The PS-SNISS 2020-2024 states that the DHIS2 platform is coordinated by a technical team and a steering committee chaired by the Secretary General of the Ministry of Health and Social Development, with the SLIS under the ministry's DGSHP and the hospital subsystem under the sector planning and statistics unit (CPS); the date is the plan's, February 2021.

The PS-SNISS 2020-2024 states that there is no budget line for the national health information system and that the units in charge mostly ask technical and financial partners to fund their activities; its performance table records a dedicated budget line as absent in 2019 and 2020, with creation of one a planned activity.

The PS-SNISS 2020-2024, dated February 2021, is a costed five-year plan of 32,916,523,000 FCFA, 54.2% of it for the health information subsystem, which schedules regular DHIS2 updates and version migration, data quality reviews in DHIS2 and DHIS2 interoperability with other platforms, with most activities financed 'Etat/PTF'.

The PS-SNISS 2020-2024 lists weak computerisation of hospitals, private ones included, for the patient record among the hospital subsystem's weaknesses, and sets targets for the proportion of first-reference and of second- and third-reference hospitals using a computerised medical record of 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% over 2021-2024, the 2019 and 2020 baselines being marked not available and ANTIM the source.

The PS-SNISS 2020-2024 records, in the minutes of the steering committee meeting of 11 December 2020, that computerisation of Mali's hospitals is coordinated by the ministry's agency ANTIM, and assigns ANTIM the activity of making the hospital computerisation software interoperable with DHIS2, financed 'Etat et PTF'.
